# regen-comments — phase internals

What each phase does inside its clean room, with per-step success criteria. Step numbers mirror the Runbook in [SKILL.md](SKILL.md). These describe the **`code` genre** in full; the `test` / `functional_test` / `example` genres reshape Step 1's triage aim and Step 4's writer shape per [SKILL.md § Targeting, genre, and scope](SKILL.md#targeting-genre-and-scope), keeping the same clean-room / verify / report / refine machinery.

### Step 0 — Voice, strip, rooms (in-session)
**Voice (first human gate):** if `--voice <key>` was given, use it; otherwise print the in-session numbered text menu (every voice + its persona + first preview sentence, `plain` marked default), wait for the user to type a number or key, and use the pick. NOT an `AskUserQuestion` — the registry overflows its 4-option cap. A run is exactly one voice, or none. (If invoked as `--create-voice`, do the registry-add flow instead and stop — no generation.)
**Strip:** run `strip.py target.py` → stripped code (comments + docstrings removed, executable code byte-identical), and capture the file's leading header (copyright/license/author) for later reattach. Set up `/tmp/regen-cr/<run>/` rooms. Copy stripped code into the code-lens / writer / judge rooms; by default copy the original (commented) file into the comment-lens room only (skipped with `--without-comment-triage`).
- **Success:** a single voice is fixed; stripped code parses and runs identically to the original.

### Step 0b — Library triage (library-aware mode, when the target is a directory)
When the target is a directory, run `regen_phase0.py` ONCE before the per-file loop: it strips the library source (clean-room — library facts come from code behavior, not comments), lays it under `lib/`, and runs the broad library triage (`library_triage.md`) as one `claude -p` → `LIBRARY_FACTS.md` (domain + cross-file contracts + glossary; same telegraphic ledger shape, at library scope). Every per-file room then gets this file: the per-file lenses **defer** to it (never re-surface a fact it already states, recording only file-specific facts or this file's application of a contract), and the writers + selector use it for **cross-file context and shared vocabulary**.
- **Success:** `LIBRARY_FACTS.md` carries the cross-file contracts + glossary as telegraphic facts; a single-file run skips this step entirely.

### Step 1 — Triage + validate (one `claude -p` from `/tmp`)
Launch one `claude -p` that runs the **triage workflow** (`triage_wf.js`): 3 code lenses on the stripped code (trap / cross-method trace / naming-vs-behavior), plus the comment lens on the commented file (runs by default; skipped with `--without-comment-triage`), then the ledger-writer merges → provisional ledger (telegraphic stubs, each with a confidence). A fixture-agnostic **validator** then checks every fact against the code and the ledger-writer re-runs against its notes until clean or 4 attempts (Step 2). The comment lens produces the **preserve lane** (live-TODOs, plus any copyright/author it flags); the copyright/license/author **header** is captured mechanically by phase 1 regardless of the flag, so it survives even `--without-comment-triage`.
- **Success:** ledger carries the non-derivable + cross-method facts as telegraphic fragments (never copyable sentences); comment-derived facts tagged and carried clean (not "grounded" against code); validator converged or `needs_user` set.

### Step 2 — Validate the ledger (inside the Step 1 workflow)
The **validator** runs against the stripped code as a stage of the triage workflow. It is **fixture-agnostic** — no trap list, no knowledge of this file's facts. For EACH ledger fact: is it true against the code? And for every fact in a correctness-critical *class* — a returned flag's referent, an inversion, a dual-role value, a boundary condition — is it stated **explicitly and unambiguously** (a reader could not invert it)? If any is wrong or under-specified, the **ledger-writer re-runs against the validator's notes (writer-only; lenses are fixed) up to 4 times**, re-validating each time. If it still won't converge, phase 1 sets `needs_user` and the orchestrator escalates to the human (Runbook step 3).
- **Success:** every ledger fact correct against the code; correctness-critical facts unambiguous; no copyable-prose stubs; converged or escalated.

### Step 3 — Picker (human gate, in-session)
Surface the **low/med-confidence** facts and any borderline **preserve** items for a keep/drop, sizing the gate to the count (Runbook step 4: 0 → skip; 1 → single-select Keep/Drop; 2–4 → multi-select `AskUserQuestion`; 5+ → numbered text list, type the numbers to drop). High-confidence facts — code- OR comment-derived — are auto-kept and never shown: a confident fact does not need a keep/drop, and surfacing them all over-involved the picker. **The human reads each fact's `gloss`** — the ledger-writer emits, per fact, both a telegraphic `stub` (writer-facing, deliberately unpasteable so a writer cannot echo it as prose) and a `gloss` (one plain-English sentence for exactly this gate). Presenting a bare stub asks the human to keep/drop compressed notation they cannot parse — the live run that surfaced "Two clock timelines" as an option proved the failure. Assemble the **final ledger** = auto-kept facts + the low/med facts the user kept (mechanically drop the rejected `- ` lines from the provisional ledger — stubs only; glosses never reach the writers). **Push back (invariant 7)** on an empty/all-unselected answer — re-confirm before dropping a batch rather than discarding it silently.
- **Success:** final ledger written; only approved facts remain.

### Step 4 — Write + select (one `claude -p` from `/tmp`)
Launch one `claude -p` that runs the **writer workflow** (`writers_wf.js`): **4 passes** (clean-room: stripped code + final ledger only), then a **best-of-4 selector**. Each writer pass uses a **lean ~230-word prompt** (a head-to-head proved lean reads *better* — more prompt degrades the comments) built on the **summarizer's own framing**: "explain in plain English what the code does; each symbol's purpose + non-obvious behavior." The spine is **behavior, not mechanism** — the docstring states **what it does and the contract a caller relies on** (never how a line computes), and a **line-level mechanic** (an inclusive boundary, a sign, a stand-in substitution) rides **only as an inline `#` comment** above its line, each fact in exactly one place. **Proportion is part of the spine:** a trivial symbol (pass-through, accessor, few obvious lines) gets one sentence; the ledger feeds the same rule upstream (a fact must survive the worth-a-sentence test — a small clean file yields a few facts, not one per symbol). It keeps three proven extras (anti-jargon, don't-restate-self-evident, no back-refs) and runs **voiceless by default**; an optional voice switches the writer to a **leaner voiced prompt** (~175 instruction words — a 2026-06-10 A/B/C/D head-to-head found the accreted rule pile flattened the voice while the lean shape kept every ledger fact and ban in a 13-arm audit; directional at n=1, confirm via the queued variance bench) that states the contract spine, pins the docstring FORM (complete summary line, no fragments, real Args/Returns/Raises where they apply), and lets the register come from the voice and its sample. A voiced run also carries the voice's **real-text sample** (the excerpt from `voice_samples/<key>.md`, prose only — attribution never reaches the prompt) framed as register grounding: absorb the rhythm, attitude, and word choice, write in your own words about this code, never reuse its phrases or subject matter, never its paragraph length or format. Both registers keep **PEP 257 shape**: a single sentence summary line, then a body of at most three or four sentences where the symbol earns one (the round33 weave-into-the-summary nudge was superseded by this shape 2026-06-10, user call; its smooth-flowing-sentences style survives on the voiceless path). The **selector** READS all 4 complete files and picks, **by number**, the single one whose comments are **best-worded at the right altitude** — alive and vivid wording, each thing said once in proportion to the symbol; a stuffed file (line-by-line narration, body paragraphs on a pass-through, one fact in several costumes) loses to one that states the contract and stops, and a flat thin file loses among the proportionate ones. **Legibility is its only floor**: a garbled, confusing, or backwards pass loses, not for being rich but for being broken; a vivid turn of phrase that reads clearly wins. It never edits or merges; phase 2 copies the chosen file verbatim, so the output is byte-identical to one writer's pass and no agent rewrite can slip in. Correctness is a **secondary sanity floor** (avoid a file that states something backwards, false, or garbled into a statement that cannot hold together), NOT a completeness gate; any residual concern rides in `pick.json` and surfaces in the report.
- **The writers carry the facts, not the selector.** The load-bearing facts ride in each pass — the caller's contract in the docstring, the line-level gotchas as inline `#` comments at their lines — so correctness is secured **upstream**. Lesser mechanics live as inline `#` comments rather than bloating the docstring, and the picker already chose which ledger facts ride.
- **Success:** one chosen pass copied to `merged.py`; code AST-identical; each docstring reads as plain prose (a substantive lead sentence, no negation-padding), line-level mechanics are inline `#` comments and the same fact is not stated in both; any selector concern surfaced.

### Step 5 — Verify (mechanical detect + clean-room polish)
Before polish, phase 2 runs the **deterministic auto-route** (`autoroute_tics.py`, no LLM): the selector picks one whole pass, so a flagged docstring can ship even when another cached pass has a clean take on that symbol. The auto-route scans the merged file for tics, voice-leaks, AND mechanical-ban violations (em-dashes, semicolons, `canonical`/`shape`, via `tics.py`'s `detect()` scan; the `tics.py <file>` CLI runs the same scan standalone) and, per flagged symbol, splices in the first other pass's take that is code-identical and scans clean on all three (class symbols: class docstring only). Substitutions are verbatim pass text (the no-rewrite guarantee holds), recorded as `autoroute` in `pick.json`, and badged on the suggested candidate in the report.
Phase 2 then runs `polish.py` — **ONE round only** — on whatever the route could not fix (symbols where every cached pass is dirty, typical of voiced registers): a clean-room `claude -p` minimally rewrites only the offending sentences (meaning + voice intact), reverting if it altered executable code. (Polish imposes no sentence-opener bans — they flatten the voice.) Violations that survive the round are written to `$RUN/bans.json` and surface as report flags with the symbol's picker badged — **the human clears the tail via pick-a-different-take or edit-it-myself**, not more LLM rounds.
- **Success:** every routable flag auto-routed (recorded + surfaced); at most one polish round spent; any surviving ban violations in `bans.json` and visible in the report next to the tic/legibility flags; code AST-identical; voice intact.

### Step 6 — Reattach (mechanical, in-session)
Run `reattach.py` to ride the **preserve lane** back onto each finished file: headers (copyright/author/license) to the top, live directives/TODOs (`# noqa`, `TODO(TICKET)`) back to their original line. A writer never rewords these.
- **Success:** preserved lines present verbatim; nothing else changed; code still byte-identical.

### Step 6b — Legibility flag (in-session)
Run `flag_legibility.py` to scan the finished file for any docstring/comment **sentence that reads awkwardly** (a clause crammed into the subject with a weak verb, a noun pile-up, a tangled construction) and write `legibility.json`. **Flag-only — it never rewrites.** A convoluted sentence is a rare, stochastic roll (a file has ~20-30 sentences, so one bad sentence per file is common while any single sentence almost never is); nothing upstream watches for it, so without this the bad roll ships. The flagger is conservative (an empty list is the normal, good result), and a flagged sentence is fixed by the human in the refine loop, not auto-reworded — the writing is already good on average, this only catches the tail.
- **Success:** `legibility.json` exists; any flagged sentences are conservative and genuinely awkward (not taste-level nits).

### Step 7 — Report (in-session)
Run `render_report.py` to build `report.html`: an **independent** plain-English summary of the file (written from the code, not the comments — so the human can check the comments against a description they did not write), the validated ledger, per-symbol before/after docstrings, the selection rationale (which whole pass won, why, and any flagged concern), and **any legibility flags surfaced up top**. Below each symbol the report opens the hood: a **picker** with the selector's winner pre-checked as *suggested*, each cached writer pass whose text differs offered as an alternative (docstring plus a full-symbol expander so inline comments are visible), an **edit-it-myself** textarea seeded with the suggested docstring, and a notes box — all persisted to localStorage so a half-finished review survives a reload, serialized by the sticky **Copy selection** bar into the paste-back blob `apply_selection.py` consumes. The static content renders without JavaScript; the picker is the only scripted layer. It **auto-opens in a browser**; also `SendUserFile` it and print the `file://` line. **Tell the human to actually open and read it** — name the changes, the verification results, and any flagged sentences so they know what to look at; do not assume they have seen it.
- **Success:** `report.html` rendered, auto-opened + surfaced, and the human pointed at it with a plain-language summary of what changed, any legibility flags, and the fact that they can pick per symbol / edit in the page and paste the blob back.

### Step 8 — Refine + apply loop (human gate; loop until Apply or Discard)
This is one **persistent loop**, not a one-shot. Each round, re-render + re-surface the report, then ask `AskUserQuestion` "What next?". Because `AskUserQuestion` allows ≤ 4 options, split it: a **round menu** (Refine a symbol · Apply · Discard; +Apply-all in library mode), and — when the human picks Refine — a *which symbol?* question (≤3 + free-text "Other") then a *what change?* question (4 opts: roll the dice · tighten · edit the facts · write it myself). **A refine never exits the loop;** only Apply or Discard do. The exits are buttons the human must press — keep looping until they do. Throughout, honor invariant 7: a lossy/risky/out-of-directive request gets a push-back with options, not blind compliance.
- **selection blob** — the batch form of refine: the human picked per-symbol takes / typed edits in the report and pasted the Copy-selection blob. `apply_selection.py parse` it, read the picks + edits + notes (invariant 7 on anything lossy or contradicted), `apply` it (each `run-N` pick is a guarded splice from the cached passes; each `edit` replaces that docstring with the human's exact text), then re-run `polish.py` + `verify_code.py` + both flaggers and re-render — the cached passes are pre-polish and no watcher ever saw this *combination* of passes whole, so the assembled file gets the full check again. Back to the round menu.
- **roll the dice** — a different take. Cheap: `splice_symbol.py` cycles the cached candidates `runs/run-1..4.py` for that symbol (its docstring + comments swap, code guaranteed unchanged). Once the four are exhausted, `regen_symbol.py` generates fresh.
- **tighten** — `tighten_symbol.py <symbol>`: shorter and denser, fact-preserving. Keeps the summary + Args/Returns/Raises + every ledger fact, cuts only wordy body prose, and prints a KEPT/DROPPED report. This is the sanctioned answer to "this is too long / drop the body" — a raw delete is lossy (it dropped a kept by-reference fact in testing), so push back and offer tighten instead.
- **edit the facts** — *drop / edit*: change `ledger_final.md`, then `regen_symbol.py <symbol>` (re-runs the writer against the edited ledger and splices only that symbol back; others stay). *add*: a **correction** goes through `stubify_fact.py` (confirmed + no concern → append stub + regen; **contradicted OR `concern` set (clearly-wrong / low-value noise) → push back (invariant 7)**, comply on confirm; unverifiable+checkable → ask for a source; else trust); a **your-own-note** is kept verbatim as `# NOTE(<initials>): …` at the symbol (ask initials; offer voiced vs verbatim; push back first if it reads as useless) — the comment lens re-harvests it later.
- **write it myself** — replace that symbol's docstring with the human's exact words.
- After any **ledger** edit, `drift_check.py` looks for OTHER symbols the change made sure-stale and offers to regen those too (never blocks the single-symbol intent).
- **Apply** — `cp $RUN/FINAL_<voice>.py <target.py>`: write the finished file onto the working tree (uncommitted, reversible) so the human reviews the diff in their editor; exit the loop. Do not commit. In **library mode** Apply advances to the next file's report+loop; **Apply all remaining** writes every remaining file unreviewed, so push back (invariant 7) and confirm the human accepts skipping review first.
- **Discard** — exit the loop, write nothing.

Every regeneration re-runs `polish.py`, and `splice_symbol.py` guards code byte-identity, so no edit can drift the code.
- **Success:** the loop exited on the human's explicit Apply (finished file written to the working tree, uncommitted) or Discard (nothing written); code still AST-identical; zero mechanical-ban violations.
